title: Expand Repeat Brackets
statement:
A string is written in a compact form: k[text] means "text written k times in a row". Blocks can be nested, and plain letters can appear anywhere between blocks.

Given such a string s, return the fully expanded text.

The input is always well formed: brackets match, every [ follows a positive whole number k (which can have several digits), digits appear only as these counts, and the text itself has only lowercase letters.

examples.why: Expand the inside first: "a3[b]" is "abbb". That whole piece is then repeated twice.
The count is 12, not 1 followed by 2. Read every digit before the bracket.

constraints: The expanded text has at most 200 000 letters
hints: When you hit a closing bracket, you need two things you saw earlier: the text built so far before the matching '[' and the count in front of it. Which structure gives back the most recent unfinished thing first?
Keep a current string and a current number. On '[', save both on a stack and start fresh.
On ']', pop the saved prefix and count, and set current = prefix + current repeated count times.

explain.intuition:
Brackets nest, and the innermost block always closes first. That is exactly the order a stack hands things back. While reading, keep the text of the block you are inside right now. When a new block opens, push what you had so far (and the count that belongs to the new block) and start an empty text for the inside.

When the block closes, the inside is finished. Pop the count and the outer text, repeat the inside, and glue it onto the outer text. That combined string becomes the current text again, one level up. It works like a parser keeping track of open tags in an HTML string.
steps: Keep cur = "", k = 0, and two stacks: saved counts and saved prefixes.
Digit: k = k * 10 + digit, so multi-digit counts build up.
Letter: append it to cur. At the end, cur is the answer.
pitfalls: Reading only one digit as the count. 12[q] needs twelve copies.
Forgetting to reset the count after pushing it, so the next block inherits an old number.
Repeating the whole string built so far instead of only the text inside the brackets.

solutions.title: Two stacks
solutions.idea: Save the outer text and the count on '['; on ']' repeat the inner text and attach it to the saved outer text.

solutions.title: Recursive descent
solutions.idea: A function reads until it meets ']' or the end and returns the expanded text. On 'k[' it calls itself for the inside.

followups: Return only the length of the expanded text, when that length can be far too large to build. What changes?
Return just the letter at position p of the expanded text without building it.
